day_shape: IAEA Board of Governors votes 23-3-8 to refer Iran to UN Security Council for first time in 20 years, Brent crosses $101, Netanyahu pledges from Syrian border to defeat Iran, CENTCOM claims 10 Iranian tankers destroyed in past week.

threads.label: IAEA refers Iran to Security Council
threads.summary: The IAEA Board of Governors adopted a US/E3-drafted resolution referring Iran's nuclear file to the UN Security Council by 23 votes to 3, with 8 abstentions; Russia, China and Niger voted against. Iran International noted it is the first such referral in 20 years, while Iran, Russia and China issued a joint statement calling the move legally baseless.

threads.label: US-Iran naval conflict and oil markets
threads.summary: CENTCOM said IRGC claims of striking two US destroyers were false and that US forces destroyed 10 Iranian tankers in the past week; IRIB reported an explosion heard from the Strait of Hormuz near Jask, and Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned strikes on Iranian tankers. Regime channels reported Brent crossing $101 and European gas up 2.3% to €75.

threads.label: Iranian domestic debate over prolonging war
threads.summary: Iran International reported moderates and former presidents Rouhani and Khatami pushing for a public say on ending the war, while a senior official said hijab enforcement has been curbed by war conditions. Regime figures including Ayatollahs Jannati and Alizadeh rejected referendum proposals and reiterated calls for jihad and resistance.

threads.label: Israeli operations on northern fronts
threads.summary: Netanyahu visited the Syrian border pledging to defeat Iran, and Defence Minister Katz messaged Syria's president from 35km away; Israeli strikes were reported in southern Lebanon's Bint Jbeil district and on a motorcycle near Harouf. UN Secretary-General Guterres called for Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon, and the Arab League reportedly adopted a resolution rejecting Hezbollah's military activities.

threads.label: Gaza strikes and post-ceasefire disputes
threads.summary: The IDF said three Hamas and PIJ weapon depots and a rocket-launch pit were destroyed in Gaza, and Palestinian media reported a strike on Shati camp; the Jerusalem Post reported Hamas is working to reclaim weapons and control despite the ceasefire. Foreign Minister Sa'ar said Israel is not planning to expel Palestinians from Gaza.

threads.label: UK and international sanctions posture
threads.summary: The FCDO republished statutory guidance for the Iran sanctions and Iran nuclear sanctions regimes and delivered a Syria statement to the September IAEA Board of Governors. The Jerusalem Post reported Turkey, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and the UAE welcomed Britain's ban on imports from Israeli West Bank settlements.

threads.label: UAE-Netanyahu October 7 warning row
threads.summary: Netanyahu instructed lawyers to file libel proceedings against Haaretz over its report that the UAE had warned him of Hamas's October 7 attack; sources told the Jerusalem Post the Biden administration was unaware of any specific UAE warning. Defa Press listed the Netanyahu UAE-warning claim among items it said had been denied in the past 24 hours.

The ministry emphasised in a statement today that this team's mission is to collect information and assess the security situation in the Strait of Hormuz. Seoul announced last week that it is reviewing various options including military action and joining the terrorist US army to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, Lee Jae-myung and Emmanuel Macron, Presidents of South Korea and France, discussed military cooperation and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz in a meeting in Paris.
